## Outline

* Remote sensing and photogrammetry: what each contributes to UAS mapping
* Why a photograph is not a map: perspective, relief displacement, orthorectification
* Overlap, stereoscopic coverage, and tie points
* Principles of Structure from Motion and bundle adjustment
* Anchoring the model: geotags, ground control points, checkpoints, RTK/PPK

## Supplemental materials

* [Structure from Motion demo](sfm_demo.qmd): interactive visualization of a UAS camera tracking ground points along a flight path
* [Aerial Photogrammetry Concepts (2016 slides)](https://ncsu-geoforall-lab.github.io/uav-lidar-analytics-course/lectures/02_Aerial_Photogrammetry_Concepts.html#/): more on the history of aerial mapping
* [Reconstruction of Palmyra from tourist photos](https://www.isprs-ann-photogramm-remote-sens-spatial-inf-sci.net/III-5/81/2016/) [@wahbeh_2016_palmyra]
* [Reconstruction of popular monuments from crowdsourced photos](https://www.isprs-ann-photogramm-remote-sens-spatial-inf-sci.net/III-3/51/2016/) [@hartmann_2016_crowdsourced]
* [Open Heritage: 3D models of iconic locations](https://artsandculture.google.com/project/cyark) (CyArk and Google Arts & Culture)
* [Introduction to Structure from Motion Photogrammetry](https://opentopography.org/workshops/GSA2021), OpenTopography short course at GSA 2021 [@opentopography_2021_sfm]
* [Multi-View Stereo: A Tutorial](http://carlos-hernandez.org/papers/fnt_mvs_2015.pdf), the standard reference on dense matching [@furukawa_hernandez_2015]

## Assignment

* [Assignment 2A: 3D reconstruction from multiple photos](assignments/assignment_2a.qmd): photograph an object, build a 3D model from the overlapping images, and report how the number and orientation of photos, lighting, and the object itself affected the reconstruction. See the assignment page for the report requirements, submission instructions, and due date.
